resources.name: ESS ServiceNow ITSM Get Request Details
resources.title: ESS ServiceNow ITSM Get Request Details
resources.description: Extend the Employee Self-Service agent to look up ServiceNow service catalog requests (REQ) and request items (RITM).
resources.summary: Extend the Employee Self-Service agent to look up ServiceNow service catalog requests (REQ) and request items (RITM).
resources.author: Dean Cron
resources.whatItIs: A Copilot Studio and Power Automate sample for the Microsoft Employee Self-Service (ESS) agent. The built-in ITSM orchestrator only handles incidents, so this adds two flows (one for the ServiceNow `sc_request` table and one for `sc_req_item`) and three topics. A single user-facing topic extracts the number from the user's message, routes RITM numbers to the request-item flow and everything else to the request flow, and shows an adaptive card with a link to open the record in ServiceNow.
whyUseIt: Let employees ask for the status of a service catalog request or request item by number.
Calls ServiceNow as the signed-in employee (on-behalf-of), so ServiceNow's own access controls decide what each person can see.
Deploy with the ESS Maker Kit or import a ready-made solution.
resources.howToUse:
1. Install the ServiceNow ITSM extension pack, deploy the ESS agent, and create a ServiceNow connection that uses on-behalf-of (invoker) authentication.
2. Deploy with the ESS Maker Kit (copy the topics and both flows into your workspace, replace the `{FLOW_GUID}` and connection reference placeholders, then push) or import `solution/ESSServiceNowITSMGetRequestDetails_1_0_0_0.zip` and create the three topics in Copilot Studio.
3. Set the `ServiceNowITSMPortalBaseURI` environment variable (for example `https://<instance>.service-now.com/esc`), turn both flows on in Power Automate, and enable parameter sharing for the ServiceNow connection in Copilot Studio.
4. Wire the topics to the flows, publish the agent, and try a prompt such as "What's the status of my request REQ0012345?" With the Maker Kit:

   ```text
   python scripts/push.py
   python scripts/push.py --repair "Get Request Details"
   python scripts/push.py --repair "Get Request Item"
   ```
prerequisites: Microsoft Employee Self-Service agent deployed
ServiceNow ITSM extension pack installed in Copilot Studio
ServiceNow connection in Power Platform configured for on-behalf-of (invoker) authentication
ServiceNowITSMPortalBaseURI environment variable set to your ServiceNow portal URL
ESS Maker Kit (for the push.py deployment path)
ServiceNow users with read access to sc_request and sc_req_item

whyUseIt: Update meeting invite bridge numbers for many users after changing your default bridge or adding local numbers.
Limit or disable call-me and dial-out destinations to control Communication Credits use.
Disable toll-free dial-in for specific users while leaving it on for others.
resources.howToUse:
1. Install the MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module (2.0.0 or later) and connect to Teams.
2. Prepare a CSV with a `UserPrincipalName` column for the bulk snippets.
3. Copy the snippet you need from the README and adjust the values, for example to change the bridge number in meeting invites:

   ```powershell
   Import-Module MicrosoftTeams
   Connect-MicrosoftTeams

   $newbridgenumber = "+15551234567"
   $updatebridgeusers = Import-Csv "C:\path\to\updatebridgeusers.csv"

   foreach ($user in $updatebridgeusers) {
       Set-CsOnlineDialInConferencingUser -Identity $user.UserPrincipalName -ServiceNumber $newbridgenumber
   }
   ```
prerequisites: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module, version 2.0.0 or later
Users enabled for Teams Audio Conferencing
CSV with a UserPrincipalName column for the bulk snippets

resources.whatItIs: A PowerShell script (BlockUsersWithoutLicense.ps1) that calls the Viva Engage network REST API with a Microsoft Entra access token to read the current per-user license enforcement state or to enforce per-user licensing for the network. whyUseIt: Check whether per-user licensing is already enforced for your Viva Engage network.

resources.howToUse:
1. Provision Viva Engage Core (recommended) or Yammer Enterprise service plans to all users. Enforcement can't be reversed.
2. Get a valid Microsoft Entra access token for a Global Administrator of the Viva Engage network.
3. Check the current state, then enforce when ready:

   ```powershell
   ./BlockUsersWithoutLicense.ps1 fetch_current_license_state "<ENTRA_ACCESS_TOKEN>"
   ./BlockUsersWithoutLicense.ps1 enforce_user_license "<ENTRA_ACCESS_TOKEN>"
   ```
prerequisites: Global administrator access to the Viva Engage network
Viva Engage Core (recommended) or Yammer Enterprise service plans provisioned to all users before enforcing
PowerShell 5.1 or later and network access to Viva Engage

resources.name: Viva Engage Community Creation App
resources.title: Viva Engage Community Creation App
resources.description: Sample Power App and Power Automate flow that create Viva Engage communities by calling the Microsoft Graph community creation API.
resources.summary: Sample Power App and Power Automate flow that create Viva Engage communities by calling the Microsoft Graph community creation API.
resources.author: Dean Cron
resources.whatItIs: An importable Power Apps solution (VivaEngageCommunityCreationApp.zip) containing a canvas app and a Power Automate flow. The app collects a community name, description, and privacy setting, and the flow gets a Microsoft Graph token with an Entra app registration and creates the community through the community creation API, with the signed-in user as owner. It is a sample and not intended for production use.
whyUseIt: See an end-to-end example of the Viva Engage community creation API behind a Power App front end.
Start from a working app and flow and adapt them to your own community creation process.
resources.howToUse:
1. Create an Entra app registration with the Microsoft Graph `Community.ReadWrite.All` and `User.Read.All` application permissions, grant admin consent, and create a client secret. Note the application (client) ID and directory (tenant) ID.
2. In Power Apps, choose Import canvas app, upload `VivaEngageCommunityCreationApp.zip`, and select or create an Office 365 Users connection.
3. Edit the app, remove and re-add the `Viva Engage CC Flow` in the Power Automate pane, and enter your values in the flow's `Get Access Token` action, which uses this request body:

   ```text
   grant_type=client_credentials
   &client_id=CLIENTID
   &client_secret=CLIENTSECRET
   &scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default
   ```

4. Turn the flow on in Power Automate, then save and publish the app. The full steps are in `AppImportInstructions.docx`.
prerequisites: Microsoft Viva Engage
Power Apps and Power Automate environment where you can import a solution
Microsoft Entra app registration with Community.ReadWrite.All and User.Read.All application permissions and a client secret
Office 365 Users connection
